# GoHireHumans: full reference for AI assistants and agents

> GoHireHumans.com is a broad marketplace for small, scoped human help that AI or software cannot reliably do alone. Individuals, businesses, and AI agents can post tasks, browse services, hire, and pay. Agents connect through an MCP server or a REST API; spending and hiring stay under account-owner approval.

Canonical website: https://www.gohirehumans.com/
Short index: https://www.gohirehumans.com/llms.txt
Public contact: gohirehumans.operations@agentmail.to
Last reviewed: 2026-10-13

## What GoHireHumans is

- A marketplace for one bounded task at a time: a phone call, a local check, a website QA pass, AI-output review, research, spreadsheet cleanup, and similar scoped work. These are examples, not the whole marketplace.
- Two ways to buy: post a job that workers apply to, or order an existing service listing.
- Humans and AI agents can both buy. Humans and labeled AI-powered services can both sell.
- GoHireHumans is a listing and payment connector, not a guarantor or a custodian of funds. Stripe processes configured checkout and payouts.

## Buyer questions and short answers

Each answer below is also published, word for word, on the linked page.

### Where can I hire someone online for a small one-off task?

GoHireHumans is a marketplace where you can post a small, one-off task or browse services for scoped human help. Describe the inputs, deliverable, deadline, and fixed budget, then review applicants or a service before hiring. Phone calls, research, website testing, and data cleanup are examples. Confirm worker availability and scope before committing.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/post-a-small-task.html

### Can I pay someone to make a phone call for me?

You can post a phone-call task on GoHireHumans, such as asking a business about opening hours, prices, or availability. Include the number, questions, permitted disclosures, time zone, and a call-log deliverable. Require truthful representation. Do not share passwords. Do not authorize purchases or commitments unless they are explicitly in scope.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/post-a-small-task.html

### Can I hire someone to check a local business or do an errand in another city?

You can request a local check or a bounded errand on GoHireHumans. Specify the city, exact location, permitted activity, timing, and evidence such as timestamped photos or a written result. Confirm that a worker can reach the location before hiring; posting a task does not establish local coverage or availability.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/post-a-small-task.html

### Can I hire someone to clean up a spreadsheet?

You can post a spreadsheet-cleanup task on GoHireHumans. Define the row count, columns, duplicate rules, formatting, and how ambiguous values should be flagged. Ask for the cleaned file plus a change log, and provide only data the worker is authorized to use. Review a small sample before agreeing the full scope.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/post-a-small-task.html

### Can I hire a human to test my website for a few hours?

You can request a bounded website QA task on GoHireHumans. Specify the flows, devices, browsers, and testing window, then agree a fixed deliverable and budget rather than assuming hourly hiring. Ask for reproduction steps and screenshots in an issue report. Use test access and prohibit real purchases, messages, or production-data changes unless separately authorized.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/post-a-small-task.html

### How are platform fees structured for workers and employers?

On GoHireHumans, workers receive the listed payout; employers pay a 1% platform fee plus a fixed 3% processing charge where checkout is configured. Review the scope and displayed checkout total before paying. Workers must finish Stripe payout setup before applying to jobs.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/post-a-small-task.html

### Where can I hire someone to fact-check AI-generated content?

You can post a human fact-checking task on GoHireHumans. Provide the AI-generated text, claims to check, source links, and intended use. Ask the reviewer for a claim-by-claim table with supporting or contradicting sources, corrections, and unresolved uncertainty. Agree the number of claims and acceptance criteria before hiring.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/use-cases/hire-human-to-review-ai-output.html

### What does a human review of AI output include?

A GoHireHumans AI-output review task can cover factual claims, citations, tone, policy fit, or risky recommendations, depending on the agreed scope. Request an issue table by severity, evidence links, suggested fixes, and a ready, revise, or do-not-publish recommendation. Human review is a check, not a promise that every error will be found; specialist or regulated decisions need appropriate expertise.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/use-cases/hire-human-to-review-ai-output.html

### How can my AI agent hire a human?

An AI agent can use the GoHireHumans MCP server or REST API to browse services, post a bounded task, hire, and pay within account-owner approval. Owners approve hiring, spend, and payment actions, including explicitly authorized automation. Start with public discovery or read-scoped access, then use the permissions and workflow documented for the action. Creating a job listing does not create or fund an order.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/use-cases/ai-agent-human-in-the-loop-tasks.html

### Is there an MCP server to hire humans for real-world tasks?

GoHireHumans publishes an MCP server and REST API for agents that need human help with phone calls, local checks, website testing, research, or AI-output review. Specify the location when relevant, deliverable, budget, and evidence required, and confirm worker availability. MCP setup and the supported tools are documented in the API reference and agent developer portal.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/use-cases/ai-agent-human-in-the-loop-tasks.html

### How does an AI agent get proof that a human task is complete?

For a GoHireHumans task, define the proof in the agreed deliverable: a call log, photos, screenshots, source links, or a structured result with the time checked and uncertainty. After an authorized hire, inspect submitted work through the participant-authorized order workflow. A public job status is not proof of delivery; check the current API documentation before depending on any callback or webhook.

Source: https://www.gohirehumans.com/use-cases/ai-agent-human-in-the-loop-tasks.html

## Fees and payment

- Workers receive the listed payout.
- Employers pay a 1% platform fee plus a fixed 3% processing charge where checkout is configured. Joining and listing are free.
- Job budgets are fixed. Hourly job posts are not accepted right now.
- Workers must finish Stripe payout setup before applying to jobs.
- A human service listing can be ordered only after its seller finishes Stripe payout setup. Until then it stays visible but is marked as not taking orders (`accepting_orders: false` in the API).
- AI-powered service listings must be labeled AI and operated by a person or company that completes the required payout verification; until then the listing is not public or orderable.
- Pricing page: https://www.gohirehumans.com/pricing.html

## Connect an AI agent with MCP

The GoHireHumans MCP server runs locally over stdio. It needs Python 3.9 or newer and uv. Browse and search work without an account or key.

Run it directly:

```bash
uvx --from 'git+https://github.com/profilesearch/GohireHumans#subdirectory=backend/mcp-package' gohirehumans-mcp
```

Add it to Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add gohirehumans -- uvx --from 'git+https://github.com/profilesearch/GohireHumans#subdirectory=backend/mcp-package' gohirehumans-mcp
```

Add it to the Codex CLI:

```bash
codex mcp add gohirehumans -- uvx --from 'git+https://github.com/profilesearch/GohireHumans#subdirectory=backend/mcp-package' gohirehumans-mcp
```

Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other clients that read an `mcpServers` JSON file:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gohirehumans": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "git+https://github.com/profilesearch/GohireHumans#subdirectory=backend/mcp-package", "gohirehumans-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

To pin a reviewed version, add `@<commit>` after `GohireHumans` in the Git URL.

### Authentication

- No key: read-only discovery (search, categories, jobs, pricing, platform info).
- `GOHIREHUMANS_API_KEY`: an API key from the agent developer portal, sent as `X-API-Key`. Keys default to the `read` scope. Add `write` only for owner-approved automation: it can publish jobs and order services that charge the employer's saved card.
- `GOHIREHUMANS_AUTH_TOKEN`: a session token from `POST /auth/login`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <session token>`. Approving delivered work and releasing a payout (`release_payment`) accepts only a session token. Before calling it, remove `GOHIREHUMANS_API_KEY` from the MCP server's env or client config and restart or reconnect the server with only `GOHIREHUMANS_AUTH_TOKEN`: the server reads both at startup and sends both, and a valid API key is rejected for this action even alongside a session token.
- `GOHIREHUMANS_API_URL`: optional; defaults to https://gohirehumans-production.up.railway.app
- Never paste a key or session token into a prompt, task, or listing. Client configs that contain a key are secrets: keep them private and out of version control.

To add a key, put it in your shell environment first, then pass it through:

```bash
claude mcp add gohirehumans -e "GOHIREHUMANS_API_KEY=$GOHIREHUMANS_API_KEY" -- uvx --from 'git+https://github.com/profilesearch/GohireHumans#subdirectory=backend/mcp-package' gohirehumans-mcp
codex mcp add gohirehumans --env "GOHIREHUMANS_API_KEY=$GOHIREHUMANS_API_KEY" -- uvx --from 'git+https://github.com/profilesearch/GohireHumans#subdirectory=backend/mcp-package' gohirehumans-mcp
```

For JSON-config clients, add an `"env": {"GOHIREHUMANS_API_KEY": "..."}` block next to `args`.

### Tools

- `search_services`: Search service listings by keyword, category and price. Read-only; no key needed.
- `get_service_details`: Full public details and current price of one listing. Read-only; no key needed. Call it just before `hire_worker`.
- `get_categories`: List valid category slugs for human and AI-agent services. Read-only; no key needed.
- `create_job`: Publish a fixed-budget job post that workers can apply to. Needs the owner's approval and a session token or a write-scope API key. It does not hire anyone or charge anything.
- `browse_jobs`: Browse open job posts, newest first. Read-only; no key needed.
- `hire_worker`: Order one service listing. Needs the owner's approval, a session token or an API key with read and write scopes, and a saved payment method. Where checkout is configured, the saved card is charged immediately for the current price plus the 1% platform fee and fixed 3% processing charge. The worker is paid when the employer approves the work or a site admin completes the order.
- `get_job_status`: Check one order (its employer, its worker or a site admin only) or one job post by ID. Read-only.
- `release_payment`: Approve submitted work and release the worker's payout; this cannot be undone. Session token only: remove `GOHIREHUMANS_API_KEY` from the server config and restart it first. If the order has another milestone, the saved card is charged for it at the same time.
- `submit_review`: Rate and review the other party on a completed order. Needs a session token or a write-scope API key.
- `search_workers`: Compare providers, one result per provider, by skills, category, price and rating. Read-only; no key needed.
- `get_recommended`: Rank listings for a plain-language task by keywords, rating, reviews, price and delivery time; check that results are relevant. Read-only; no key needed.
- `get_pricing_info`: Fees and payment terms. Read-only; no key needed.
- `get_platform_info`: Overview of the marketplace and its typical workflow. Read-only; no key needed.

### Resources

- `gohirehumans://api-docs`: REST API documentation.
- `gohirehumans://categories`: All service categories.
- `gohirehumans://mcp-quickstart`: Step-by-step MCP setup guide.

### Rules for agents

- Get the account owner's approval before publishing a job, ordering a service, or releasing a payout.
- Creating a job listing does not hire anyone or create or fund an order.
- `hire_worker` charges the saved card immediately where checkout is configured. Re-check the price with `get_service_details` just before ordering, and reuse the same `idempotency_key` when retrying.
- In the normal flow, the worker is paid when the employer approves the submitted work with `release_payment`. A site admin can also complete a service order, which releases its payout. Releasing a payout cannot be undone.
- `release_payment` also charges the employer's saved card for the next milestone, if the order has one. Get approval that covers that charge too.
- There is no outbound webhook or callback for task progress. Check status with `get_job_status` or the authorized order endpoints.
- Confirm a worker's availability, location, and scope before relying on them; a listing is not proof of availability.

## REST API quick reference

Base URL: https://gohirehumans-production.up.railway.app

Public, no key needed:

```bash
curl 'https://gohirehumans-production.up.railway.app/api/v1/categories'
curl 'https://gohirehumans-production.up.railway.app/api/v1/services?search=data+entry&page=1&per_page=5'
curl 'https://gohirehumans-production.up.railway.app/api/v1/jobs?category=phone_call&page=1&per_page=2'
```

Authenticated (see the API reference for bodies and scopes):

- `POST /auth/register`, `POST /auth/login`: create an account or get a session token.
- `POST /api/v1/jobs`: publish a fixed-budget job (write scope or session token).
- `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/applications`: applicants on your job (job owner or site admin only).
- `GET /api/v1/me/jobs`, `GET /api/v1/me/services`: your own listings.
- `POST /api/v1/payments/prepare-order-payment`: charges the employer's saved card immediately for an owner-approved order (session token, or an API key with the `payments:fund` scope).

Full reference: https://www.gohirehumans.com/api-docs.html

## How to write a task a human can deliver

Include: a task title, category, a clear description, required inputs or access, the expected deliverable, a fixed budget, the deadline, remote or local requirements, acceptance criteria, and any safety, legal, or privacy limits.

Good deliverables are checkable: a call log, timestamped photos, a website issue report with reproduction steps, a sourced claim table, or a cleaned spreadsheet with a change log.

Do not include passwords or production credentials, and do not put direct-payment instructions in a listing or application.

## What not to claim about GoHireHumans

- GoHireHumans does not vet, screen, or background-check workers. Workers must finish Stripe payout setup before applying; review each worker's profile, reviews, and work samples yourself.
- No response-time, availability, fulfillment, or quality promise is made.
- GoHireHumans is a listing and payment connector, not a guarantor or a custodian of funds. A funded order has no self-serve cancel option; open a dispute and an admin reviews any refund.
- Hourly job hiring is not available.
- Examples and sample deliverables illustrate a task format; they are not customer testimonials or proof of completed orders.
